items.a: No water system is. USP and Ph. Eur. set limits for water, not approvals for equipment. The factory acceptance test (FAT) proves function before shipping. The site acceptance test (SAT) and operational qualification (OQ) prove it on your feed water.

items.q: Our auditor expects stainless. Will PP pass?
items.a: It can: no rule requires stainless. 21 CFR 211.65 and GUI-0001 C.02.005 ask for surfaces that do not react, add or absorb, and survive sanitizing. WHO TRS 1033, 7.2.1, generally recommends 316L or polyvinylidene chloride (PVDC) and does not name polypropylene (PP). We answer its list point by point.

items.q: Which edition of each standard do you design to?
items.a: The edition in force when you approve the functional specification. If a text changes mid-project, as Ph. Eur. 0008 did, we assess it under change control.

items.q: Does our corporate engineering standard replace yours?
items.a: No, it adds to this list. We write it into the functional specification and flag any conflicting clause before detailed design, not at installation qualification (IQ). A standard that requires stainless rules out polypropylene, unless it allows exceptions.

items.q: Who registers our pressure equipment, and when?
items.a: The safety authority of each province where the item is used, before it is built. Each pressure-rated item needs a Canadian registration number (CRN) under CSA B51, unless exempt. [Aquemi CRN process and provinces covered]
